and `-RCDevAutoZoomAccept YES`, with which the Auto Zoom sheet presses its own
Zoom once its first plan exists, so a proof can drive Clip ▸ Auto Zoom… to its
edit (spec §11 CU-76);
and `-RCDevSpeedUpTypingAccept YES`, with which the Speed Up Typing sheet
presses its own Apply once its first plan with ops exists (spec §11 CU-93);
and `-RCDevRetimeAccept YES`, with which the Retime Range sheet presses its
own Apply so a proof can drive Clip ▸ Retime Range… to its edit (spec §11
CU-90 (d)); and `-RCDevSwitchSpeakerAccept YES`, with which the Switch by
Speaker sheet presses its own Switch once its first plan exists (spec §11
SW-26); and `-RCDevFollowAccept YES`, with which the Follow Subject sheet
presses its own Follow once it is first enabled (spec §11 VR-29 (h)); and
`-RCDevVerticalAccept YES` (or `in-place`, which unticks Make a copy first),
with which the Make Vertical Version sheet presses its own Make once it is
first enabled (spec §11 VR-39 (h)); and `-RCDevDerivedHidden YES`, with which `new_project_from_range` opens its
document with no window (`display: false`), so a proof can see the windowless
door (spec §11 CJ-52); and `-RCDevExportFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`, the same for an
`ExportWriter` export's pumps, spec §11 #378), which
Distribution does not. `rc_op_names`
and the catalog are the authority for the counts; the parity check compares
them at startup. `render_frame` writes a PNG and returns its path; `export`
puts the job on the Export Queue and answers an `export_id` at once, and
`export_status` answers it until `done` (`mcp.py`'s `export_with` waits; spec
§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. <?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. 1 # 04 — implementation notes: docs site in the Boppa Llewyn design system 2 3 Worktree `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-ai-docs-int` (branch `ai-docs-int`). No commit. The index is untouched: the font deletions are unstaged working-tree deletions, and the new files are untracked. 4 5 ## What was done (in the Approach's order) 6 7 1. **Fonts.** Fetched the Google Fonts CSS2 response (Geist and Geist Mono, `wght@100..900`, desktop Chrome UA, no other headers) into a fresh scratch folder. Downloaded the four `latin`/`latin-ext` WOFF2 files and Geist's `OFL.txt` (vercel/geist-font `main`). `file` reports WOFF2 for all four: Geist latin 29,288 B, latin-ext 16,540 B, Geist Mono latin 23,108 B, latin-ext 14,712 B. The licence reads "Copyright 2026 The Geist Project Authors". Copied them into `public/fonts/` under the spec's four names and deleted the twelve Cormorant and IBM Plex files. `OFL.txt` now has a short header naming the two families and their files, then Geist's licence text verbatim. 8 2. `font-face.css` has four rules: `'Geist'` and `'Geist Mono'`, `100 900`, normal style, swap, and the `unicode-range` copied from the response (`latin-ext` now ends at `U+20AD-20C4`, as Google serves it). `tokens.css` is the handoff file copied whole. Prettier only changed `"` to `'` in the two font stacks. `boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` is byte-identical (`cmp`). `astro.config.mjs` changed in: the logo, the `customCss` order, the two preloads, the comments, and `expressiveCode.styleOverrides` (`borderRadius: '10px'`, `borderColor`, `codeLineHeight: 'calc(22 / 14)'`, and the five `frames.*` title-bar keys). In the built `ec.*.css` they show as `--ec-brdRad:10px`, `--ec-codeLineHt:calc(22 / 14)`, `--ec-frm-edTabBarBg:var(--bl-surface)` and so on. 9 3. **`boppa-llewyn.css` rewritten**, in this order: 10 - header comment; 11 - type and layout `--sl-*` on plain `:root`, so FeatureIndex's 68rem width still wins; 12 - one colour mapping on `:root, ::backdrop`, plus the dark backdrop overlay; 13 - headings (600, a line height per level); 14 - the eyebrow group, links, focus outline, 120 ms transitions and the reduced-motion rule; 15 - the Site layer, one block per README part: header, search, icon buttons, menu button, sidebar, ToC and mobile ToC, page opener, body, Steps, tables, asides, code, kbd, buttons, cards and link cards, pagination, footer meta, splash. 16 - The hero band uses `box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax` plus `clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax)`. The old border-top and padding on the splash's markdown are gone; every splash `h2` (its `.sl-heading-wrapper`) takes the `--bl-line` rule, with 64 px margin above it and 64 px padding below the rule, as in the mock's `.splash h2`. 17 - The code background, active-tab background and title type are set in CSS, by overriding Expressive Code's `--ec-frm-*` custom properties unlayered. 18 4. **`frame-job.css`:** Shot (with the framed window: `.fj-window`, `.fj-window-bar`, `.fj-window-dot`, `.fj-window-title`), AtAGlance and the feature index are restyled. 19 - **Shot.astro:** a `frame` prop. With it, the figure gets `fj-shot--framed`, no max-width, and a window holding an `aria-hidden` bar (three dots and `siteTitle`) and both images. 20 - **index.mdx:** `frame` added to the editor-window Shot. 21 - **SiteTitle.astro:** the lockup as the Interfaces section gives it. The mark is 32 × 32 with `alt=""`. `.company` and `.sep` hide below 50rem. 22 - **ThemeSelect, PageTitle, Hero:** only the style blocks and header comments changed. 23 5. README "Theme" section rewritten, then `prettier --write` run over the README, styles, fonts, components and config. 24 25 ## Deviations and judgement calls 26 27 - **The theme toggle's icon size is set in `boppa-llewyn.css`, not `ThemeSelect.astro`.** Starlight's `Icon` sets its svg's `width`/`height` in `@layer starlight.components`, which comes after `starlight.core`, so a rule in the component's `starlight.core` style block can't resize the icon. The 18 px size is in the "Icon buttons" block of `boppa-llewyn.css` (`.theme-toggle svg`), with a comment saying why. 28 - **Header order.** The mock puts the theme toggle before GitHub, with no divider. Starlight renders GitHub first and draws a divider. `.social-icons { order: 1 }` and `::after { content: none }` match the mock without a component override. 29 - **Footer meta below the pagination.** Starlight renders the meta first. `footer .meta { order: 1 }` puts it 32 px below the pagination, under a hairline. An empty meta (the splash) is hidden with `:empty`. 30 - **The ToC column's own left hairline is removed** (`.right-sidebar { border-inline-start: 0 }`). The mock has only the list's rail. 31 - **Opener.** The hairline Starlight draws between the title panel and the body is removed. The description-to-body gap is 16 px, as in the mock. 32 - **Eyebrow to title.** The README says 12 px, and that is what the site uses. The mock renders closer, because its `.prose p { margin: 16px 0 0 }` overrides `.eyebrow`'s bottom margin (a quirk of the mock). 33 - **Aside icons.** Tip, caution and danger icons use the `-high` colour, as the README says. The note's icon uses `--sl-color-blue` (ink-muted), as drawn in the mock. Its title is `-high` (ink). 34 - **Nested sidebar groups** (Colour → Grade, Target, Check, Reuse) also render as eyebrows, as before. Their summaries get 6 px block padding so that closed groups don't crowd. The 8 px gap under a group label is on the open list, so a closed group doesn't add it. 35 - **Pagination keeps Starlight's arrow icons**, in `--bl-ink-subtle` (README: "keep Starlight's own icons"). The `
` is hidden and `.link-title` is made a block, giving the 2 px label-to-title gap. 36 - **Feature index count:** mono 12 px `--bl-ink-subtle` with no uppercase (README wording). It was uppercase before. 37 - **Overflow fix outside the README's list.** The 390 px check failed on `/features/` (scrollWidth 405): a `kbd` reading "⌘ while dragging" in a Where cell couldn't wrap. Added `.fj-features td kbd { max-width: 100%; height: auto; min-height: 1.5rem; white-space: normal }` in `frame-job.css` (feature index block). All six pages now measure 390/390. 38 - The hero tagline is 17/26 below 50rem (README "lede"). The mock keeps it at 19/30 on a phone. 39 - The site's splash content is 1120 px wide (spec: "full 1120 px container width"). The mock's is 1056 px, because it pads inside its 1120 px box. 40 41 No file outside the spec's Files list was touched. 42 43 ## Comparisons (shots in `/Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/docs-theme-redesign/shots/`) 44 45 All 24 site captures and 8 mock captures are named `site---.png` and `mock---.png`, with side-by-side crops in `shots/crops/`. 46 47 - **Content page, light and dark at 1440:** `site-splitting-{light,dark}-1440.png` against `mock-content-{light,dark}-1440.png`. 48 - These match part for part: the 64 px header, lockup, badge, the 260 × 36 search with small keys, the ghost icon buttons, sidebar eyebrows and the current pill, eyebrow, h1, lede, AtAGlance, Steps squares and connector, the table rule weights, and the ToC rail. 49 - Content differences are the pages' own: the real page has no Shot, and its AtAGlance says "Agent tools". 50 - **Splash, light and dark at 1440:** `site-splash-{light,dark}-1440.png` against `mock-splash-{light,dark}-1440.png`. They match: the band, eyebrow, 64 px title, tagline, three buttons, the 192 px mark, the framed window (dots, centred title, large shadow), the muted requirements paragraph, the hairline before "Start here", and the link cards. 51 - **Phone (500 px):** `site-splash-light-500.png` against `mock-splash-light-500.png` (crop `crops/splash-500-pair.png`), and `site-splitting-dark-500.png` against `mock-content-dark-500.png` (crop `crops/content-500-pair.png`). 52 - They match: the mark sits above the text at 96 px, the text is start-aligned, the company name and slash are hidden, and the menu and search are 36 px ghost buttons. 53 - The site also shows Starlight's mobile ToC strip, which is kept by design. 54 - **Asides:** `site-animate-a-grade-{light,dark}-*.png` (tip, caution) and `site-synchronize-audio-{light,dark}-*.png` (note, tip). Crops: `crops/aag-steps-tip.png` and `crops/aag-dark.png`. Each aside has a full tint, the icon, a sentence-case title, a muted body, no border and 10 px corners. `:::danger` is checked only by reading the CSS (red-low/red-high mapping), as the spec says. 55 - **Code:** `site-cursor-files-*.png` (crop `crops/cursor.png`, a plain block) shows the sunken background, `--bl-line` border and 10 px corners. An extra capture, `extra-connect-client-dark-1440.png` (crop `crops/connect.png`), shows a terminal frame with its title bar on the surface. 56 - **Feature index:** `site-features-{light,dark}-{1440,500}.png` (crops `crops/features.png`, `crops/features-500.png`). 57 58 ## 390 px widths (scrollWidth clientWidth) 59 60 | Page | Widths | 61 |---|---| 62 | `/` | 390 390 | 63 | `/editing/splitting/` | 390 390 | 64 | `/color/animate-a-grade/` | 390 390 | 65 | `/audio/synchronize-audio/` | 390 390 | 66 | `/recording/cursor-files/` | 390 390 | 67 | `/features/` | 390 390 (405 390 before the kbd fix) | 68 69 `dist/width.html` was deleted afterwards. The server, `python3 -m http.server 50422` on 127.0.0.1, was stopped. 70 71 ## Checks 72 73 All Full commands pass; outputs are in `04-checks.txt`. Build: 366 pages, links valid. `format:check`, `docs_site_proof` (0 problems) and `name_residue` all exit 0. Both greps print nothing, and `dist/fonts` holds exactly the four Geist WOFF2 files and `OFL.txt`. Targeted `check-pages` on `index.mdx`: 1 page, 0 problems. 74 75 Nothing is still failing. 76 77 ## Owed (orchestrator) 78 79 The `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` "Where things are" edits listed in the spec's Out of scope: the `src/styles/` row, and the new `src/assets/` row. 80

36	## What changes, file by file
37	
38	All paths are under `docs/site/`.
39	
40	| File | Change |
41	|---|---|
42	| `src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css` | Rewritten on the new tokens: the old `--bl-*` block is replaced by `tokens.css`, the `--sl-*` mapping follows the table below, and every rule below "Site layer" is restyled to the mock. Keep its structure (tokens, mapping, base rules, then the parts Starlight's variables can't reach) and its rule of preferring CSS over overrides. |
43	| `src/styles/frame-job.css` | `Shot`, `AtAGlance` and the feature index restyled (below). |
44	| `src/fonts/font-face.css`, `public/fonts/` | Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex removed; Geist and Geist Mono added (below). |
45	| `astro.config.mjs` | `logo` points at the blocks mark; the two `preload` links name the Geist files; `expressiveCode.styleOverrides` follow "Code blocks". |
46	| `src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | New: copied from this folder. `src/assets/logo.svg` (the Frame Job mark) stays, for the splash hero and anywhere the product is shown. |
47	| `src/components/SiteTitle.astro` | The lockup (below). |
48	| `src/components/Shot.astro` | One new optional prop, `frame`, for full-window captures (below). |
49	| `src/content/docs/index.mdx` | The editor-window `Shot` gains `frame`. No other content changes. |
50	| `README.md` ("Theme") | Rewritten to describe the new system: the families, the palette pair, the files. |
51	| `CLAUDE.md` | The `src/fonts/, public/fonts/` row names the new faces, if it names them. |
52	
53	`ThemeSelect.astro`, `PageTitle.astro` and `Hero.astro` keep their markup; they change through CSS only. `public/favicon.svg` stays the Frame Job icon, because the tab belongs to the product.
54	
55	## Fonts
56	
57	- **Geist** (variable, weights 100 to 900) and **Geist Mono** (variable, 100 to 900), both under the SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Take the `latin` and `latin-ext` WOFF2 subsets from Google Fonts, as the current faces were. Self-host them in `public/fonts/` as now, split by `unicode-range` in `font-face.css`.
58	- Replace `public/fonts/OFL.txt` with Geist's licence text (it names the Geist Project Authors). Delete every Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex file and rule; nothing uses them afterwards.
59	- Preload the two `latin` files, Geist and Geist Mono: the page's first screen has both (the header's version badge and the page eyebrow are mono).
60	- `--sl-font: var(--bl-font-sans)` and `--sl-font-mono: var(--bl-font-mono)`. The stacks in `tokens.css` fall back to the Mac's own San Francisco and SF Mono. Remove `--bl-font-display` and every rule that sets headings in it.
61	
62	## Starlight's colour variables
63	
64	Map these in both looks; each value is a token from `tokens.css`, so the light and dark values come from the token, not from this table. Starlight's grey scale runs from strongest ink to page background.
65	
66	| Starlight variable | Token | Notes |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `--sl-color-white` | `--bl-ink` | Headings, strongest text |
69	| `--sl-color-gray-1` | `--bl-ink` | |
70	| `--sl-color-gray-2` | `--bl-ink-muted` | Descriptions, card bodies |
71	| `--sl-color-gray-3` | `--bl-ink-subtle` | Eyebrows, captions, meta |
72	| `--sl-color-gray-4` | `--bl-line-strong` | Control borders, hover borders |
73	| `--sl-color-gray-5` | `--bl-line` | |
74	| `--sl-color-gray-6` | `--bl-surface` | Cards, header, AtAGlance |
75	| `--sl-color-gray-7` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | Hovers, code, kbd wells |
76	| `--sl-color-black` | `--bl-bg` | |
77	| `--sl-color-text` | `--bl-ink` | Body copy |
78	| `--sl-color-text-accent` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Links |
79	| `--sl-color-text-invert` | `--bl-on-accent` | Text on the accent |
80	| `--sl-color-accent-low` | `--bl-accent-soft` | Current sidebar item |
81	| `--sl-color-accent` | `--bl-accent` | Primary button, ToC rail |
82	| `--sl-color-accent-high` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Text on `accent-low` |
83	| `--sl-color-bg` | `--bl-bg` | |
84	| `--sl-color-bg-nav` | `--bl-surface` | Solid; the header no longer blurs |
85	| `--sl-color-bg-sidebar` | `--bl-bg` | Separated by a `--bl-line` hairline |
86	| `--sl-color-bg-inline-code` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | |
87	| `--sl-color-bg-accent` | `--bl-accent` | |
88	| `--sl-color-hairline`, `-light`, `-shade` | `--bl-line` | |
89	| `--sl-color-backdrop-overlay` | light `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.4)`, dark `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` | |
90	| `--sl-color-blue-low` / `blue` / `blue-high` | `surface-sunken` / `ink-muted` / `ink` | Note |
91	| `--sl-color-purple-low` / `purple` / `purple-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Tip |
92	| `--sl-color-green-low` / `green` / `green-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Success badge |
93	| `--sl-color-orange-low` / `orange` / `orange-high` | `caution-soft` / `caution` / `caution` | Caution |
94	| `--sl-color-red-low` / `red` / `red-high` | `danger-soft` / `danger` / `danger` | Danger |
95	| `--sl-shadow-sm` | `--bl-shadow-card` | |
96	| `--sl-shadow-md`, `--sl-shadow-lg` | `--bl-shadow-window` | The search dialog only |
97	
98	Every text pairing here holds at least 4.5:1 in both looks, and every control border and focus ring at least 3:1. Don't introduce a colour that isn't a token.
99	
100	## Type
101	
102	| Where | Style | Size / line height | Weight | Tracking |
103	|---|---|---|---|---|
104	| Splash hero title | `display` | 64 / 64 px (40 / 42 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.035em |
105	| Page title (`h1`) | `heading-1` | 40 / 44 px (32 / 36 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.03em |
106	| `h2` | `heading-2` | 28 / 34 px | 600 | −0.02em |
107	| `h3`, card and pagination titles | `heading-3` | 20 / 28 px | 600 | −0.01em |
108	| `h4` | | 17 / 24 px | 600 | 0 |
109	| Page description, hero tagline | `lede` | 19 / 30 px (17 / 26 below 50rem) | 400 | 0 |
110	| Body | `body` | 16 / 26 px | 400 | 0 |
111	| Sidebar links, tables, asides, AtAGlance | | 15 px, 20–24 px leading | 400 | 0 |
112	| ToC, captions, meta, footer | `small` | 14 / 20 px | 400 | 0 |
113	| Eyebrows: page eyebrow, sidebar group labels, ToC label, table headers, AtAGlance terms | `eyebrow` | 12 / 16 px mono, uppercase | 500 | 0.06em |
114	| Inline code, code blocks | `code` | 14 / 22 px mono | 400 | 0 |
115	
116	So `--sl-text-body: 1rem`, `--sl-line-height: 1.625`, `--sl-text-h1: 2.5rem`, `--sl-text-h2: 1.75rem`, `--sl-text-h3: 1.25rem`, `--sl-text-h4: 1.0625rem`, `--sl-line-height-headings: 1.1`, `--sl-text-code: 0.875rem`. Headings are `--sl-color-white`; there's no bold 700 and no italic heading anywhere.
117	
118	## Corners, borders and depth
119	
120	| Radius | Used on |
121	|---|---|
122	| `--bl-radius-sm` 6 px | `kbd`, inline code, sidebar links, the Steps markers, the feature filter's input |
123	| `--bl-radius-md` 10 px | Buttons, the search field, icon buttons (menu, theme, GitHub), asides, code frames, AtAGlance, Shot |
124	| `--bl-radius-lg` 16 px | Cards, link cards, pagination links, the framed Shot, dialogs, the mobile ToC dropdown |
125	| `--bl-radius-pill` | The header's version badge |
126	
127	Hairlines are `--bl-line`; a hover strengthens a border to `--bl-line-strong`. Nothing lifts, scales or moves on hover.
128	
129	## The parts, in order down the page
130	
131	**Header** (64 px). Solid `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` bottom border, no blur. Gaps of 24 px.
132	
133	- **Lockup** (`SiteTitle.astro`): the blocks mark at 32 px, then **Boppa Llewyn** in Geist 600 17 / 24 px at −0.02em, a `/` in `--bl-ink-subtle` weight 400, the site title (**Frame Job**) in weight 500, and the version badge. Gap 8 px. The badge is mono 500 12 / 16 px, `--bl-ink-subtle`, padding 2 px 8 px, pill-shaped, drawn with an inset 1 px `--bl-line-strong` ring. Below 50rem the company name and the slash hide, leaving the mark, **Frame Job** and the badge. The lockup still links to the docs home.
134	- **Search** (desktop): a 260 × 36 px field on `--bl-surface-sunken` with a `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, the placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle` 14 px, and the ⌘K keys as small `kbd` (20 px tall). Below 50rem it's a 36 px icon button.
135	- **Theme toggle and GitHub link**: 36 px square ghost buttons, `--bl-radius-md`, icon in `--bl-ink-muted`; hover `--bl-surface-sunken` with `--bl-ink`. The toggle keeps its two-state behaviour and its storage key.
136	- **Menu button** (below 50rem): the same 36 px ghost button, keeping the 44 px hit area the current CSS gives it.
137	
138	**Sidebar** (280 px). Background `--bl-bg`, a `--bl-line` hairline on the right, padding 32 px 16 px 48 px 24 px.
139	
140	- Group labels: `eyebrow`, `--bl-ink-subtle`, 8 px above the links, 28 px between groups.
141	- Links: 15 / 20 px, `--bl-ink-muted`, padding 6 px 10 px, `--bl-radius-sm`, 1 px apart. Hover: `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-ink`. Current page: `--bl-accent-soft` background, `--bl-accent-ink` text, weight 550. Keep the existing guard so hover doesn't override the current item.
142	
143	**Page opener** (`PageTitle.astro`, through CSS). The content column is 680 px (`--bl-prose-width`), 56 px from the header.
144	
145	- Eyebrow: `eyebrow` in `--bl-accent-ink`, 12 px above the title. This is the page's one accent-coloured label.
146	- Title: `heading-1`.
147	- Description: `lede` in `--bl-ink-muted`, 16 px below the title.
148	
149	**Body.** Paragraphs and lists 16 px apart; list items 6 px apart. Links are `--bl-accent-ink`, no underline until hover (1 px underline, 3 px offset). `h2` has 48 px above and 12 px below; `h3` 32 px above and 8 px below.
150	
151	**AtAGlance** (`.fj-glance`). `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 32 px above. A two-column grid (terms at their own width, 24 px gap, 10 px between rows). Terms are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`; values 15 / 24 px, menu paths bold, keys as `kbd`, tools as inline code at 13 px.
152	
153	**Shot** (`.fj-shot`). The capture at up to half its pixel width, as now, with a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md` and `--bl-shadow-card`, 32 px above. The caption is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, centred, 10 px below.
154	
155	- **New `frame` prop**: for a full-window capture (a `*.window` screen), `<Shot name="04-editor.window" frame alt="…" />` draws the capture in a window frame instead:
156	  - a 36 px title bar on `--bl-surface` with three 12 px dots in `--bl-line` (not traffic-light colours) and the window title centred in 13 px weight 500 `--bl-ink-subtle`;
157	  - `--bl-radius-lg`, no border, and `--bl-shadow-window`, the site's only large shadow.
158	- Use `frame` on the splash's editor window. Leave partial captures (sheets, inspectors) unframed.
159	
160	**Steps** (Starlight's `<Steps>`). Each number sits in a 28 px square:
161	
162	- `--bl-surface-sunken` fill, 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-sm`;
163	- the number in mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`;
164	- a 1 px `--bl-line` connector down to the next square.
165	
166	Text is indented 48 px, with 20 px between steps.
167	
168	**Tables**. Full width, 15 / 22 px. Headers are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`, 10 px above a `--bl-line-strong` rule. Cells are padded 10 px 12 px 10 px 0, with a `--bl-line` rule under each row. Code in a cell doesn't wrap, as now.
169	
170	**Asides** (`:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution`, `:::danger`). Each is the system's callout:
171	
172	- a full-tint background, the icon, and the type's word as the title;
173	- no border and no left accent bar;
174	- `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 24 px above;

## What changes, file by file

All paths are under `docs/site/`.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css` | Rewritten on the new tokens: the old `--bl-*` block is replaced by `tokens.css`, the `--sl-*` mapping follows the table below, and every rule below "Site layer" is restyled to the mock. Keep its structure (tokens, mapping, base rules, then the parts Starlight's variables can't reach) and its rule of preferring CSS over overrides. |
| `src/styles/frame-job.css` | `Shot`, `AtAGlance` and the feature index restyled (below). |
| `src/fonts/font-face.css`, `public/fonts/` | Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex removed; Geist and Geist Mono added (below). |
| `astro.config.mjs` | `logo` points at the blocks mark; the two `preload` links name the Geist files; `expressiveCode.styleOverrides` follow "Code blocks". |
| `src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | New: copied from this folder. `src/assets/logo.svg` (the Frame Job mark) stays, for the splash hero and anywhere the product is shown. |
| `src/components/SiteTitle.astro` | The lockup (below). |
| `src/components/Shot.astro` | One new optional prop, `frame`, for full-window captures (below). |
| `src/content/docs/index.mdx` | The editor-window `Shot` gains `frame`. No other content changes. |
| `README.md` ("Theme") | Rewritten to describe the new system: the families, the palette pair, the files. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The `src/fonts/, public/fonts/` row names the new faces, if it names them. |

`ThemeSelect.astro`, `PageTitle.astro` and `Hero.astro` keep their markup; they change through CSS only. `public/favicon.svg` stays the Frame Job icon, because the tab belongs to the product.

## Fonts

- **Geist** (variable, weights 100 to 900) and **Geist Mono** (variable, 100 to 900), both under the SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Take the `latin` and `latin-ext` WOFF2 subsets from Google Fonts, as the current faces were. Self-host them in `public/fonts/` as now, split by `unicode-range` in `font-face.css`.
- Replace `public/fonts/OFL.txt` with Geist's licence text (it names the Geist Project Authors). Delete every Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex file and rule; nothing uses them afterwards.
- Preload the two `latin` files, Geist and Geist Mono: the page's first screen has both (the header's version badge and the page eyebrow are mono).
- `--sl-font: var(--bl-font-sans)` and `--sl-font-mono: var(--bl-font-mono)`. The stacks in `tokens.css` fall back to the Mac's own San Francisco and SF Mono. Remove `--bl-font-display` and every rule that sets headings in it.

## Starlight's colour variables

Map these in both looks; each value is a token from `tokens.css`, so the light and dark values come from the token, not from this table. Starlight's grey scale runs from strongest ink to page background.

| Starlight variable | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--sl-color-white` | `--bl-ink` | Headings, strongest text |
| `--sl-color-gray-1` | `--bl-ink` | |
| `--sl-color-gray-2` | `--bl-ink-muted` | Descriptions, card bodies |
| `--sl-color-gray-3` | `--bl-ink-subtle` | Eyebrows, captions, meta |
| `--sl-color-gray-4` | `--bl-line-strong` | Control borders, hover borders |
| `--sl-color-gray-5` | `--bl-line` | |
| `--sl-color-gray-6` | `--bl-surface` | Cards, header, AtAGlance |
| `--sl-color-gray-7` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | Hovers, code, kbd wells |
| `--sl-color-black` | `--bl-bg` | |
| `--sl-color-text` | `--bl-ink` | Body copy |
| `--sl-color-text-accent` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Links |
| `--sl-color-text-invert` | `--bl-on-accent` | Text on the accent |
| `--sl-color-accent-low` | `--bl-accent-soft` | Current sidebar item |
| `--sl-color-accent` | `--bl-accent` | Primary button, ToC rail |
| `--sl-color-accent-high` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Text on `accent-low` |
| `--sl-color-bg` | `--bl-bg` | |
| `--sl-color-bg-nav` | `--bl-surface` | Solid; the header no longer blurs |
| `--sl-color-bg-sidebar` | `--bl-bg` | Separated by a `--bl-line` hairline |
| `--sl-color-bg-inline-code` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | |
| `--sl-color-bg-accent` | `--bl-accent` | |
| `--sl-color-hairline`, `-light`, `-shade` | `--bl-line` | |
| `--sl-color-backdrop-overlay` | light `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.4)`, dark `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` | |
| `--sl-color-blue-low` / `blue` / `blue-high` | `surface-sunken` / `ink-muted` / `ink` | Note |
| `--sl-color-purple-low` / `purple` / `purple-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Tip |
| `--sl-color-green-low` / `green` / `green-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Success badge |
| `--sl-color-orange-low` / `orange` / `orange-high` | `caution-soft` / `caution` / `caution` | Caution |
| `--sl-color-red-low` / `red` / `red-high` | `danger-soft` / `danger` / `danger` | Danger |
| `--sl-shadow-sm` | `--bl-shadow-card` | |
| `--sl-shadow-md`, `--sl-shadow-lg` | `--bl-shadow-window` | The search dialog only |

Every text pairing here holds at least 4.5:1 in both looks, and every control border and focus ring at least 3:1. Don't introduce a colour that isn't a token.

## Type

| Where | Style | Size / line height | Weight | Tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Splash hero title | `display` | 64 / 64 px (40 / 42 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.035em |
| Page title (`h1`) | `heading-1` | 40 / 44 px (32 / 36 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.03em |
| `h2` | `heading-2` | 28 / 34 px | 600 | −0.02em |
| `h3`, card and pagination titles | `heading-3` | 20 / 28 px | 600 | −0.01em |
| `h4` | | 17 / 24 px | 600 | 0 |
| Page description, hero tagline | `lede` | 19 / 30 px (17 / 26 below 50rem) | 400 | 0 |
| Body | `body` | 16 / 26 px | 400 | 0 |
| Sidebar links, tables, asides, AtAGlance | | 15 px, 20–24 px leading | 400 | 0 |
| ToC, captions, meta, footer | `small` | 14 / 20 px | 400 | 0 |
| Eyebrows: page eyebrow, sidebar group labels, ToC label, table headers, AtAGlance terms | `eyebrow` | 12 / 16 px mono, uppercase | 500 | 0.06em |
| Inline code, code blocks | `code` | 14 / 22 px mono | 400 | 0 |

So `--sl-text-body: 1rem`, `--sl-line-height: 1.625`, `--sl-text-h1: 2.5rem`, `--sl-text-h2: 1.75rem`, `--sl-text-h3: 1.25rem`, `--sl-text-h4: 1.0625rem`, `--sl-line-height-headings: 1.1`, `--sl-text-code: 0.875rem`. Headings are `--sl-color-white`; there's no bold 700 and no italic heading anywhere.

## Corners, borders and depth

| Radius | Used on |
|---|---|
| `--bl-radius-sm` 6 px | `kbd`, inline code, sidebar links, the Steps markers, the feature filter's input |
| `--bl-radius-md` 10 px | Buttons, the search field, icon buttons (menu, theme, GitHub), asides, code frames, AtAGlance, Shot |
| `--bl-radius-lg` 16 px | Cards, link cards, pagination links, the framed Shot, dialogs, the mobile ToC dropdown |
| `--bl-radius-pill` | The header's version badge |

Hairlines are `--bl-line`; a hover strengthens a border to `--bl-line-strong`. Nothing lifts, scales or moves on hover.

<style is:global>
	@layer starlight.components {
		.sl-steps {
			--bullet-size: calc(var(--sl-line-height) * 1rem);
			--bullet-margin: 0.375rem;

			list-style: none;
			counter-reset: steps-counter var(--sl-steps-start, 0);
			padding-inline-start: 0;
		}

		.sl-steps > li {
			counter-increment: steps-counter;
			position: relative;
			padding-inline-start: calc(var(--bullet-size) + 1rem);
			/* HACK: Keeps any `margin-bottom` inside the `<li>`’s padding box to avoid gaps in the hairline border. */
			padding-bottom: 1px;
			/* Prevent bullets from touching in short list items. */
			min-height: calc(var(--bullet-size) + var(--bullet-margin));
		}
		.sl-steps > li + li {
			/* Remove margin between steps. */
			margin-top: 0;

Every `--bl-*` token the CSS, components and config use is defined in `tokens.css`. No old token is left. Expressive Code's styles are in `@layer starlight.components`, so the unlayered `--ec-frm-*` overrides in `.expressive-code` do take effect.

## Findings

### 1 — should-fix
- **Where:** docs/site/src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css:638
- **What:** The unlayered `.sl-markdown-content li + li { margin-top: 0.375rem }` beats Starlight's layered `.sl-steps > li + li { margin-top: 0 }` (`starlight.components`). That adds 6 px between steps: they sit 26 px apart instead of the README's and mock's 20 px, and the gap in the connector grows from 4 px to 10 px.
- **Fix:** Exclude steps from the rule (`li + li:not(:where(.not-content *, .sl-steps > *))`), or add `.sl-steps > li + li { margin-top: 0 }` in the Steps block.

### 2 — nit
- **Where:** docs/site/src/styles/frame-job.css:67-71
- **What:** `.fj-window-title`'s `margin-right: 3.25rem` (52 px) leaves out the 8 px flex gap between the last dot and the title. The left side is 60 px, so the "centred" title sits 4 px right of the bar's centre, and the comment's arithmetic is off by the same amount.
- **Fix:** Use `margin-right: 3.75rem` (3 × 12 + 3 × 8) and correct the comment.

verdict: fix-required

   - Fix: use `3.75rem` and correct the comment.
